Portrait des cinq candidats à la success: Profiles of the five candidates vying to succeed Valérie Plante as leader of Projet Montréal
Le 15 mars prochain, Montréal découvrira: On March 15, Montréal will find out who will succeed Valérie Plante as leader of Projet Montréal.
De gauche à droite et de haut en bas: Gr: From left to right and top to bottom: Gracia Kasoki Katahwa, Laurence Lavigne Lalonde, Guedwig Bernier, Luc Rabouin, Ericka Alneus, candidates for the leadership of Projet Montréal. Photos and montage: La Converse.
À fin janvier et en février, j’ai rencon: In late January and in February, I met with the five candidates for the Projet Montréal leadership: Ericka Alneus, Gracia Kosaki Katahwa, Guedwig Bernier, Laurence Lavigne Lalonde and Luc Rabouin. One of these five people will become Montréal’s next mayor.
Dès le départ, cette course a piqué ma c: From the start, this race piqued my curiosity: for the first time, three of the five candidates are Black. That diversity marks a turning point, not only at Projet Montréal, but also in Montréal’s political landscape.
Cependant, en préparant mes entrevues, j: However, as I prepared my interviews, I quickly felt a certain unease. I wanted to address crucial topics that are absent from the election platforms: gun violence, police violence, and so on. These issues, which nevertheless concern many Montrealers, seemed to have been set aside by the candidates. I brought them up anyway!
Ce reportage a également été un défi per: This story was also a personal challenge: interviewing politicians for the first time demands rigorous preparation. In that regard, I have to say that, despite their varied backgrounds, there are many similarities in what they say. All of them come out of Projet Montréal, and they have mastered the art of communication, but their answers sometimes stayed vague, with a lot of words but few concrete proposals.
Un autre défi qu’ont posé ces entrevues: Another challenge posed by these interviews, conducted ahead of the official campaign, was the reluctance of some candidates to reveal their platforms before nominations closed. So, although the conversations were recorded on video, we had to wait for the election platforms to be published to get a clearer picture of the candidates’ commitments. What’s more, some platforms remain incomplete on their respective websites.
Rappelons que les élections auront lieu: As a reminder, the election will take place on March 15. So here is an overview of each candidate’s proposals.
Le 15 mars prochain, Montréal découvrira: On March 15, Montréal will find out who will succeed Valérie Plante as leader of Projet Montréal. The leadership race, launched on February 3, is now in full swing.
La Converse a donc invité dans ses burea: La Converse therefore invited the five candidates in the running to its offices. Each laid out their ambitions, looked back on their path and explained why they believe they are best qualified to lead the party that has been running the city since 2017.
Sur papier, leurs propositions se rejoig: On paper, their proposals overlap: ecological transition, decentralizing resources toward the east end of the city, fighting the homelessness crisis by increasing the supply of affordable housing, and so on. Yet beyond these shared commitments, differences emerge.
Pour mieux les cerner, nous avons égalem: To better understand them, we also questioned the candidates on issues that are often set aside, including systemic racism and gun violence.
<strong>Ericka Alneus : « La gardienne d: Ericka Alneus: “The guardian of the city’s soul”
Originaire des Cantons-de-l’Est et issue: Originally from the Eastern Townships and from a Haitian family, she has devoted more than 10 years to the community sector and to non-profit organizations, working notably with the Y des Femmes de Montréal and Pour 3 Points. She has also sat on various boards of directors, including the Conseil de presse du Québec, Concertation Montréal and the Carrefour d’aide aux nouveaux arrivants.
<strong>Guedwig Bernier : Le défenseur d: Guedwig Bernier: The champion of diversity and finances
Moins connu du grand public, Guedwig Ber: Less well known to the general public, Guedwig Bernier nevertheless played a key role within Projet Montréal as its president from 2020 to 2024. His term was marked by a commitment to inclusion and diversity, which helped pave the way for candidacies from racialized communities, including those of Ericka Alneus and Gracia Kasoki Katahwa, in the leadership race – a first for the party.
En dehors de son engagement municipal, G: Outside his municipal involvement, Guedwig Bernier has been sales and marketing director at C3F Télécom for nearly 2015.
Le candidat à la chefferie affirme voulo: The leadership candidate says he wants to make financial management a priority, notably by seeking to reduce the costs of major construction projects through stronger collaboration with the private sector.
<strong>Gracia Kasoki Katahwa : L’infirm: Gracia Kasoki Katahwa: The nurse serving the City
Première mairesse noire de Côte-des-Neig: The first Black mayor of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (NDG), Montréal’s most populous borough, Gracia Kasoki Katahwa sits on the City of Montréal’s executive committee. She is responsible there for human resources as well as the fight against racism and systemic discrimination, and she acts as associate councillor for reconciliation with Indigenous peoples.
Née en République démocratique du Congo: Born in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and arrived in Quebec in the late 1980s, she grew up in Sainte-Foy. She graduated in nursing from Université Laval in 2009 and settled in NDG in 2010. She worked as a nurse manager at the Jewish General Hospital and has been active in the Secrétariat international des infirmières et infirmiers de l’espace francophone and the Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers du Québec.
Mairesse de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-E: Mayor of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension since 2021 and a member of the executive committee, Laurence Lavigne Lalonde is responsible for files related to ecological transition and urban agriculture, in addition to overseeing the Espace pour la vie museum complex. She presents herself as “the candidate of change, not continuity.”
Ancienne intervenante en santé mentale,: A former mental health worker, she has also worked abroad with NGOs, including Oxfam-Québec in Peru, an experience she describes as decisive for her political engagement, since it led her to run in the 2013 municipal elections.
Maire du Plateau-Mont-Royal, Luc Rabouin: Mayor of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Luc Rabouin has experience in economic management and urban development. Before getting involved in municipal politics, he worked at the Caisse d’économie solidaire and the Centre d’écologie urbaine de Montréal. Since 2023, he has been chair of the City of Montréal’s executive committee, where he is also responsible for finance. Luc Rabouin presents himself as the candidate of stability.
